title: Why does an AI invent details?
intro: A short explainer video with two questions along the way.
transfer: In the next AI summary at work, mark every concrete detail: date, number, name, decision.

scenes.caption: A language model writes word by word. At each step it picks a word that fits the text so far.
After “The team meets next …”, “Monday” fits very well. Whether it is true, the model does not check.
If the day is missing from the note, the model fills the gap with something plausible. But plausible does not mean supported.
That is why you check every concrete detail against the source: date, number, person, decision.

options: The note explicitly names a Monday
The word fits the start of the sentence
Teams usually meet on a Monday
questions.explanation: The model picks what fits the language well. Whether the source covers it is another question.

questions.prompt: What do you check first in an AI summary?
options: Whether spelling and grammar are right
Concrete details such as dates and names
questions.explanation: Concrete details are the places where gaps get filled with made-up content.

title: When does the team meet?
intro: Is every sentence of the AI summary supported by the note?
transfer: In your next meeting summary, check every date: is it in your notes like that?

note: The day of the week is still open.

summary.explanation: The note only says “next week”. The day of the week is explicitly open.
summary.hint: How does the AI know the meeting is on Monday?
summary.correction: The team meets next week. The exact day is still open.

title: The new screens
intro: Is every sentence of the AI summary supported by the note?
transfer: In AI texts, watch for dates that depend on a condition. Is the condition still there?

note: The new screens will be delivered as soon as the supplier confirms.
IT will then install them in one afternoon.

summary.text: IT installs the screens in one afternoon.
The screens will be delivered on 14 March.
summary.explanation: No delivery date is given anywhere. The delivery depends on a confirmation that is still missing.
summary.hint: What has to happen before a delivery date is fixed?
summary.correction: The screens will be delivered as soon as the supplier confirms. That is still open.

title: Budget and deadline
intro: This time more than one sentence may be unsupported.
transfer: Before you forward AI meeting minutes, write open decisions explicitly as “open”.

note: Whether the budget will be approved is still open.

summary.text: Nora is responsible for the documentation.
summary.explanation: Nora writes the documentation, which covers “responsible”.

summary.text: Nora delivers the documentation by Friday.
summary.explanation: According to the note, no deadline was agreed.
summary.hint: Which deadline was agreed for the documentation?
summary.correction: Nora writes the documentation. The deadline is still open.

summary.explanation: According to the note, the approval is still open. The AI turns an open question into a decision.
summary.hint: Has the budget already been decided?
summary.correction: The budget approval has not been decided yet.

title: Who does what?
intro: This time more than one sentence may be unsupported.
transfer: In the next AI task list, check the name and every “if” for each task.

note: Julia checks the numbers if Amir is finished by Wednesday.
Amir sends the documents to the customer.

summary.explanation: According to the note, Amir prepares the presentation.
summary.hint: Who prepares the presentation according to the note?

summary.explanation: The note ties this to a condition: only if Amir is finished by Wednesday.
summary.hint: Does the note say this without any ifs or buts?
summary.correction: Julia checks the numbers if Amir is finished by Wednesday.

summary.text: Amir sends the documents to the customer.
summary.explanation: According to the note, Amir does the sending.

title: The pilot project
intro: Several details may have changed. Check each sentence on its own.
transfer: Read an AI summary once only for numbers, and once only for “if” and “provided that”.

note: The pilot project starts in the second quarter, provided that data protection agrees.
The costs will be estimated in May.

summary.text: The costs will be estimated in May.
The pilot project starts in the second quarter.
summary.explanation: The condition “provided that data protection agrees” is missing. This makes the start sound decided.
summary.hint: Under which condition does the project start?
summary.correction: The pilot project starts in the second quarter, provided that data protection agrees.

summary.hint: How many sites does the note name?

title: Where does this number come from?
intro: Work out with the AI how to check a claim from an AI text.
transfer: When an AI text names a study or a number: find the original source before you pass the number on.

content.goal: At the end you write your own checking rule for numbers and studies in AI texts.
content.aiRole: You are a learning coach. The learner should learn to check a number or study from an AI text. Ask questions instead of giving away the solution: who did the study? Where can you find it? Does the number really appear there like that? After three answers, ask the learner to put their own checking rule into one sentence.
content.opening: Look at the sentence on the right. What would you need to know before using this number in a presentation?

material.title: From an AI chat (made up)
lines: “According to a study by the University of Zurich, 73% of employees are more productive with AI.”

criteria.label: Find the original source
criteria.hint: Who did the study, and where can you find it yourself?

criteria.label: Check the number at the source
criteria.hint: Does the number appear in the study exactly like that, and what was measured?

fallbackReplies: Good question. How could you find out whether this study really exists?
Suppose you find the study. What is the first thing you check there about the number?
Now sum it up in your own checking rule: what do you do before you pass on a number from an AI text?
Thanks. Keep this rule. You can finish the lesson now.
